text:
aina: sketch: avoid a broad runtime shim. build a slim gateway "compat router" that does 3 things only: header normalize, envelope unwrap, and small backward-field aliases. low-risk and easy to retire.

sam: agree on small scope. question: how do we detect when aliases hide real contract errors?

maria: telemetry answer: add shim.trace header and emit per-field alias metrics: alias.apply.count, alias.error.count, alias.null.count. alert if alias.error.rate > 0.3% for 24h.

aina: lifecycle idea: 1) client opt-in via X-RI-Compat=1 2) run shim for opt-ins only 3) after 28d with low error rates, flip a limited opt-out cohort 4) schedule retirement at 84d post-majority opt-out.

tom: implementation notes: lazy body parse (only when header present), tiny rule-engine (yaml driven), 10ms transform budget, circuit-breaker if transform latency >20ms for 5s window.

lane: SDKs: ship 2-line adapter snippets and a CLI helper to set tenant opt-in from console for customers who can't change clients.

ops-bot: canary deployed compat-router v0.1 to prod-canary (traffic=1%). Logs -> /infra/gw/compat-router/2026-03-23/

aina: action items: sam->sdk snippets + CLI opt-in; maria->metrics + alerts; tom->cb+perf budget; lane->migration playbook for CS. reconvene in 7 days for canary review. :thumbsup:
